summary: The frozen checker correctly distinguishes the original patch and constant-capacity canonical-loop variants, but the completed six-case boundary diagnostic exposes unsound suppression and equivalent-form instability. Repair the general bound proof and its control-flow use, not any named fixture. (1) A syntactic X-1 loop bound is not evidence of the accessed object's capacity: when capacity is unavailable or a pointer alias hides it, do not return safe merely because subtraction by one appears. Resolve array declarations/aliases when justified, otherwise retain a conservative warning rather than claiming a bounds proof. (2) The inherited conditionContainsLookAheadGuard treats all relational directions and logical OR as safe: derive whether the branch actually bounds the same array/index. A guard true only at an unsafe index, or a safe disjunct joined by an unconstrained OR, must not suppress a real warning. (3) Semantically equivalent canonical loop tests (strict/non-strict and reversed operands) and safe early-continue/break guards should agree. Verify that a guard applies to this access on all relevant paths, rather than using source order alone. Preserve the AST-based checker architecture, variable declaration identity, capacity/type extraction, normal loop and look-ahead relation, and no function/file/identifier allowlists. Preserve the original Linux vulnerable-side hit and fixed-side silence. All checker edits must be emitted by the model and compile under Clang 18. This is a separate development continuation, never a replacement for any frozen main-cohort result. Do not read diagnostic fixture files or hard-code their constants; correct the mechanism from this diagnostic description, the patch, and attached analyzer evidence. Explain assumptions and remaining unsupported cases in the final message.
